title: Gradient Dynamics and η-Stationarity Theorem
claim: Level 2 dynamics: dX/dt = W·∇χ(X) + η(X,t). W = mobility operator (acts only through gradient). η = external source term (acts at zero slope). Lean-verified: if ∇χ=0 and W·0=0 and η≠0, then Ẋ≠0. This proves escape initiation only — no trajectory, no basin, no convergence. Global annealing theorem is OPEN. η=grace and W=will are bridge identifications, not theorems.
assumptions: Level 1 canonical form χ = C_W[∏ X_i] exists as the landscape
W and η are postulated first-order open gradient dynamics, not uniquely forced
definitions: W: mobility operator, [W] = s⁻¹, placeholder W(x) = w₀·(1−R_agency(x))
η: external source term, [η] = s⁻¹, state- and time-dependent
negative_guards: Global convergence/annealing is OPEN, not a textbook application.
η=grace and W=will are bridge claims, not theorems. Lean verifies structure, not naming.
This is escape initiation only. No trajectory, basin departure, or finite displacement claimed.
kill_conditions: Exhibit a system at ∇χ=0 with nonzero η that does NOT produce nonzero velocity under the declared axioms.
Show that the gradient dynamics are the uniquely forced form (would upgrade from chosen model to necessity).
